name: Integrity
label: Victory
lede: It started as a fake band a Cleveland teenager invented on T-shirts, and became the darkest, most metal thing on Victory Records, with a pen pal named Charles Manson.

eras.title: A fake band made real
eras.text: Before Integrity existed, Dwid Hellion printed its merch. The Cleveland teenager invented bands for fun, and one of them, Integrity, was billed as the most violent straight edge band alive. In 1988 he made it real, and its first album split hardcore down the middle.

years.h: Dwid Hellion turns his invented band Integrity into a real one
years.p: After Die Hard broke up, Dwid Hellion recruited Die Hard guitarist Aaron Melnick, drummer Tony "Chubby Fresh" Pines and bassist Tom Front, and gave them a name he'd already put on shirts.
years.xp:
As a teenager in Cleveland, Dwid Hellion made up bands, designed their merch and spread their backstories by word of mouth and calls to radio shows. One was Integrity, pitched as a straight edge band so dark and violent it would attack drinkers at shows.

The logo came from a secondhand bookstore: Hellion found a book called Integrity and lifted the lettering off its cover. When Die Hard ended in 1988, he built a real band around the fiction.

years.h: A middle schooler takes over Integrity's bass
years.p: Tom Front quits after the Harder They Fall demo. Aaron Melnick's younger brother Leon, still in middle school, replaces him, and Chris Smith arrives from False Hope on second guitar.

years.h: Those Who Fear Tomorrow on Overkill Records
years.p: Integrity's debut bolts metal guitar solos and chugging riffs onto hardcore with end-of-the-world lyrics. Critics panned it and warned it would ruin hardcore. It became a blueprint for metalcore.
years.xp:
Wikipedia calls the reception universally negative. The same record was later picked for Loudwire's 2020 list of the Top 25 Metalcore Albums of All Time.

Around the same time Tony Pines left the drum stool; David Nicholi Araca took over before Mark Konopka came in from Outface.

eras.title: Holy terror on Victory
eras.text: With the Melnick brothers, Chris Smith and Mark Konopka, Integrity signed to Victory Records and made three albums in three years. The sound got bigger and stranger, and Dwid Hellion's world of cults, occult texts and Charles Manson moved to the center.

years.p: A stopgap EP between Integrity's Overkill debut and the Victory years; the Hooked, Lung, Stolen Breath Cunt EP follows in 1994.

years.h: Mark Konopka joins Integrity on drums from Outface
years.p: Mark Konopka completes the line-up of Dwid Hellion, Aaron and Leon Melnick and Chris Smith that fans still call the classic Integrity.
The classic line-up's first album for Victory. Decibel inducted it into its Hall of Fame in 2013, calling it the landmark work of a heretical catalog.

years.h: Charles Manson endorses Humanity Is the Devil
years.p: Integrity's second Victory album draws on the beliefs of the Process Church of the Final Judgement, and Charles Manson, writing to Dwid Hellion from prison, endorsed it.
years.xp:
Dwid Hellion kept up a personal relationship with Charles Manson and released recordings Manson had made in prison. Manson turns up again and again as a subject in Integrity songs.

Hellion has described Manson as a political prisoner and a religious martyr. Some sources also tie Hellion, under the name Jack Abernathy, to the Holy Terror Church of Final Judgment, a Process Church splinter group; Wikipedia presents that only as a claim.

years.h: Seasons in the Size of Days, the last classic-line-up album
years.p: Integrity's third Victory album in three years, and the last with Aaron and Leon Melnick, Chris Smith and Mark Konopka until they regrouped in 2013.

eras.title: Integ2000, then Belgium
eras.text: The classic line-up fell apart, and Dwid Hellion rebuilt Integrity with two members of Mushroomhead and a new name. Two more Victory albums followed, then Hellion moved the whole operation to Belgium.

years.h: The Melnicks leave; Mushroomhead's Feltons make it Integ2000
years.p: With Aaron and Leon Melnick gone, Dwid Hellion hires brothers Dave and Steve Felton of Cleveland's Mushroomhead and bassist Craig Martini, and renames the band Integ2000.
The Integ2000 line-up's album, released the same year as the Final Taste of Every Sin EP.

years.h: The Felton brothers exit, and Integ2000 is Integrity again
years.p: Dave and Steve Felton leave after one album and Dwid Hellion drops the Integ2000 name.

years.h: Closure, Integrity's fifth and final Victory album
years.p: Five straight Integrity albums on Victory end here. Invisible Oranges critic Neill Jameson later heard a Southern Gothic streak in Closure.

years.h: Integrity moves to Belgium and makes To Die For
years.p: MTV and Cleveland.com reported Integrity's relocation to Belgium. To Die For, sold as a comeback on Deathwish Inc., brings founding drummer Tony Pines back.

eras.title: The classic five, one more time
eras.text: Integrity kept going on smaller heavy labels, and in 2013 the Systems Overload line-up got back in a room for the first time in two decades. Relapse Records now carries the catalog, and Dwid Hellion is still the only constant.

years.p: Integrity's second album for Deathwish Inc., the label run by [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]]'s Jacob Bannon, one of the bands that name Integrity as an influence.

years.cap: The Systems Overload line-up at A389 X Bash, 2014
years.h: The Systems Overload line-up plays again at A389 X Bash
years.p: Dwid Hellion, Aaron and Leon Melnick, Chris Smith and Mark Konopka play together and sell the new 7th Revelation: Beyond the Realm of the VVitch EP at the show, weeks before its February 7 release on A389.
years.xp: The five had started recording together in 2013, their first work as a unit in more than twenty years. A389 Bash was the annual festival run by Pulling Teeth guitarist Domenic Romeo, who joined Integrity's touring line-up in 2014.

years.h: Howling, For the Nightmare Shall Consume on Relapse
years.p: A concept album about the painter Francis Bacon taking part in a séance and coming away able to see demons.

years.h: Relapse gathers the archive on All Death Is Mine: Total Domination
years.p: A Relapse compilation of Integrity's archival material, while Dwid Hellion keeps rotating new guitarists into the band.
